contradictions.title: Force-push after a rebase

sides.says: push, and after a rebase use --force-with-lease
rebase if the branch is behind
pr_creation pushes with a plain git push -u
no execute push path force-pushes
rebase currency is deliberately advisory

code.says: pushes an explicit refspec and never with a force option
pre_pr_evidence assumes history is final before it; a later rebase leaves its referents unchecked

decision.context: phase-6-pr.md, which /work-on loads at pr_creation and /execute loads at every ci_monitor visit, tells the agent to rebase when behind and push with --force-with-lease. The /work-on template pushes plainly, /execute says nothing it runs force-pushes, and push-and-record.sh refuses a force push.
decision.problem: An agent following phase-6 either gets a rejected push under /execute or rewrites a shared branch; under /work-on a rebase after pre_pr_evidence means the gate judged a tip that no longer ships.

options.name: Never rebase at PR time and never force-push
options.why: Simplest and matches the code today, but a branch that falls behind main stays behind until a person merges main in.

options.name: Rebase if behind, before verification, with a plain push only
options.why: Keeps the no-force rule true for both callers and every gate sees the tip that ships; the rebase moves earlier in /work-on.

options.name: Allow --force-with-lease inside push-and-record.sh, leased on expected_head
options.why: Keeps rebase-then-push working, but rewrites history on a branch several children commit to, which the autonomy section says needs a person.

decision.reason: It is the only option that keeps /execute's no-force guarantee and /work-on's gate evidence both true.

contradictions.title: Retry caps

sides.says: after 2 blocking_retry outcomes the next pass must escalate
escalate after 2+ retry cycles
escalate after 2+ retry cycles
no cap
analysis: up to 3
implementation: up to 3
CI: ask the user after 2-3 iterations
retry up to 3

code.says: every retry edge is unconditional; nothing counts visits
ci_monitor fix pushes go through push-and-record.sh with no counter

decision.context: The review panels, analysis, implementation, PR creation and CI loops each state a limit somewhere, the limits differ (2, 2+, 3, 2-3, none), and nothing in koto counts visits. The CI line tells the agent to ask the user, which /execute's --auto mandate forbids.
decision.problem: The agent has no single cap to apply, the panel cap's scope (per panel or shared) is unstated, and under --auto the CI instruction is unfollowable.

options.name: State each cap once, in the looping state's directive
options.why: One shared panel cap of 2 blocking retries across the three panels, 3 for analysis, implementation and PR creation, 3 fix pushes for CI then failing_unresolvable, never ask under --auto. The directive is what the agent reads when it decides.

options.name: Have koto count visits and enforce the caps
options.why: Enforced rather than stated, but needs koto support that does not exist for this yet.

options.name: Drop the caps
options.why: Removes the contradiction by removing the limit; loops are then bounded only by the agent's judgment.

decision.reason: It gives every loop one number in the place the agent reads it, and removes the --auto violation without waiting on koto. These directive caps are temporary: when koto enforces retry caps from its attempt counts, the numbers stay the same and the directive prose becomes a deletion candidate.

contradictions.title: A CI fix ends the run without re-checking CI

sides.says: monitor until all checks pass
output is a PR with passing CI
done directive assumes green CI
CI green is gate-enforced
directive points the agent at failing_fixed

code.says: failing_fixed routes to done with no gate
the fallback edge also reaches done

decision.context: /work-on promises a PR with passing CI, but ci_monitor's failing_fixed outcome and its fallback edge go to done without re-checking CI.
decision.problem: A run can end reporting success on red or unfinished CI; which behavior is intended decides whether the run stops or keeps polling.

options.name: failing_fixed loops back to ci_monitor and the fallback goes to done_blocked
options.why: Enforces the skill's own contract at the cost of one more poll per fix.

options.name: Keep the routing and correct the prose to say CI is not re-checked
options.why: No behavior change, but the output contract gets weaker.

decision.reason: The promise of passing CI is what callers rely on, and the cost is one poll.

contradictions.title: Cross-issue context is built but nothing reads it

sides.says: before each child, concatenate earlier children's summaries into current-context.md
spawn_and_await points at cross-issue-context.md
do not inspect children
the closed write-target set has no loose file at the checkout root

code.says: children receive only task variables; koto schedules them

decision.context: /execute tells the agent to build current-context.md from completed children's summaries before each child, but koto schedules the children, no /work-on file reads that file, and only evals assert it.
decision.problem: Deleting the step removes a capability the skill advertises; keeping it leaves an instruction with no effect and a stray file in the work tree.

options.name: Delete the step
options.why: Honest about what runs today; drops the advertised carry-forward.

options.name: Wire /work-on's analysis phase to read it, built outside the work tree
options.why: Makes the capability real; needs a template change in both skills.

options.name: Leave it
options.why: No work, but the instruction keeps claiming an effect it does not have.

decision.reason: Carry-forward is listed as a capability and the evals assert it; if the wiring cannot land soon, deleting beats prose with no effect.

contradictions.title: Child skills run their own approval, push and pull-request steps under /scope

sides.says: /brief asks for approval even when both reviewers pass
/brief pushes and runs gh pr create
/prd asks for approval and creates a PR
/prd creates a branch when on an unrelated one and transitions the brief
/design commits, pushes and creates a PR
/design asks Plan or Approve only
/plan asks about an upstream issue and runs gh issue edit
nothing pushes during the chain
closed write-target set; the publish script's gh calls are the only gh writes
children leave Draft/Proposed and the parent approves

code.says: /plan hard-stops unless the DESIGN is already Accepted
/scope detects a reject only through the child's discard commit

decision.context: Each child skill runs its own approval prompt, status transition, commits and, for /brief, /prd and /design, a push and a pull request, and none of those steps checks the parent_orchestration sentinel. /scope promises one push and one PR at exit and a closed write set. The dispatch reference says children should leave artifacts unapproved for the parent, but /design and /plan require their upstream already Accepted and /scope never transitions anything.
decision.problem: Under /scope the children push and open PRs /scope says never happen, and the reference that defines child behavior under a parent describes a flow that would stall the chain.

options.name: Children keep their verdict and status transition but skip push, PR, cleanup commit, branch creation and routing prompts under the sentinel
options.why: Under --auto the child takes the recommended approval and says so. The dispatch reference is rewritten to match. Smallest change that makes every stated promise true.

options.name: Parent-delegated approval as the dispatch reference describes
options.why: Adds a per-hop approval and transition to /scope and changes /design's and /plan's preconditions.

options.name: Keep today's behavior and drop /scope's one-push promise
options.why: No child change, but a no-intent /scope run then pushes, and an intent run can open two PRs.

decision.reason: It keeps the per-artifact gate the next hop depends on and removes only the steps that collide with /scope's publish model.

contradictions.title: /design's inline-decision fallback under a parent

sides.says: under a parent, /design resolves decisions inline and records decision_provenance
always spawn one /decision agent per question
Phase 2 delegates each question to the decision skill

code.says: a /scope fixture carries decision_provenance: inline-resolved

decision.context: The dispatch reference lets /design resolve decisions inline when a parent routes decisions back to itself; /design's own Phase 2 always spawns /decision, nothing defines when the fallback applies, and the provenance field is in no format reference or validator.
decision.problem: Whether a /scope run bypasses /decision is left to the agent's judgment.

options.name: Delete the fallback
options.why: Every run spawns /decision agents; most expensive.

options.name: Make it checkable: under the sentinel, standard-tier questions resolve inline and critical ones go to /decision; add the field to the format reference
options.why: A condition the agent can check, and irreversible questions still get the full treatment.

options.name: Resolve every question inline under /scope
options.why: Cheapest; loses /decision's rigor on the questions that need it.

decision.reason: It turns an unstated judgment into a checkable rule without giving up /decision where it matters.

contradictions.title: /plan files issues and a milestone under --auto without approval

sides.says: an activation that files issues requires human approval
multi-pr step 7.1 files issues and a milestone with no approval step

decision.context: /plan's own rule says filing issues needs human approval, but the multi-pr path and single-pr-with-tracking file issues and a milestone with no approval step, and under --auto the tracking question is never asked. /scope forwards --auto to /plan on intent runs.
decision.problem: An unattended run can create GitHub issues and a milestone that nobody approved.

options.name: Approval on every filing path; under --auto, file only when CLAUDE.md declares a Tracking Level header, else emit an issueless PLAN with outlines
options.why: Makes the stated rule true and reuses the rule the coordinated path already follows.

options.name: Never file under --auto or under a parent
options.why: Simplest; a caller who wants issues runs /plan again interactively.

options.name: Keep the behavior and rewrite the rule to allow it
options.why: No behavior change; unattended filing becomes intended.

decision.reason: It keeps filing possible where a repository has opted in and otherwise produces a PLAN the validator already accepts.

contradictions.title: /scope's abandonment exit writes a Draft PLAN that fails L01

sides.says: abandonment triggered at /plan writes the PLAN at Draft with a marker
a committed Draft PLAN is a violation
a committed PLAN at status Draft is a violation

code.says: the single-pr posture requires Active; L01 has no abandonment exemption

decision.context: An abandonment exit triggered while /plan is running force-materializes the PLAN at Draft at its canonical path; the same reference and /plan's rules say a committed Draft PLAN is a violation, and the lifecycle check has no exemption.

options.name: The validator skips a PLAN carrying the abandonment marker
options.why: Keeps the partial PLAN; adds an exemption to the validator.

options.name: Abandonment never writes a PLAN, only the upstream artifacts
options.why: No exemption; the partial PLAN's content is lost unless the upstream drafts carry it.

decision.reason: It needs no validator exemption, and a PLAN that never finished has little a later run could reuse.

decision.problem: Whether the running agent may approve its own continuation after an upstream change is a question of who approves, and no code enforces either side.

options.name: The running agent resolves in place when it judges intent unchanged, and escalates otherwise
options.why: Fewer stops, but the agent judging the change is the one whose work it would invalidate.

decision.reason: The classification is itself the judgment that matters, and the agent making it is the party being checked; SKILL.md already says there is no separate team lead under /scope.
